scoring.partial_credit: Award proportionally within each point. Citation credit is independent of substantive correctness.

substantive_logic_points.criterion: Covers checkpointer validation and, only in strict MessagePack mode, collection of state/input/output/context/node/branch schema types, allowlist construction, and application to the checkpointer.
Explains interrupt normalization and validation, including graph source/target/entrypoint/interrupt failures, then distinguishes root-only versus non-managed output and stream channel selection.
Explains generated default error-handler creation, the reserved-name conflict, exclusion of handler nodes from handler routing, and construction of the node-to-handler map.
States that existing per-node values win; retry and timeout defaults apply to all nodes, while cache defaults and error-handler routing apply only to regular nodes.
Covers CompiledStateGraph configuration, serde allowlist, START and user-node attachment, output/state mapper selection, ordinary and waiting edges, branches, and final compiled.validate return.

citation_format_points.criterion: Material claims have inline `relative/path.py:start-end` citations that resolve at the frozen revision.
Citations cover validation/serialization helpers and compiled-graph assembly, not only the compile declaration.

substantive_logic_points.criterion: Covers checkpointer resolution/allowlisting, missing-checkpointer and empty-superstep/update failures, and checkpoint-namespace subgraph delegation or failure.
Explains saved checkpoint migration/copy versus empty creation, prior versions and step derivation, config merging, and channel/managed-value reconstruction.
Explains END task clearing including pending/null writes and update checkpoint, plus INPUT mapping, its single-update constraint, input checkpoint metadata, put_writes, and no-input-writes failure.
Explains `__copy__` validation and fork checkpoint, optional grouped follow-up updates, next-task ID reuse by node occurrence, and recursive ordinary superstep application.

Covers task-ID discovery, single-update as_node inference and ambiguity, multi-update requirements, node/writer validation, writer invocation context, and provided/prepared/deterministic task-ID precedence.

Distinguishes pre-checkpoint non-PUSH writes and post-checkpoint PUSH writes; covers apply_writes, delta snapshot planning and metadata, checkpoint persistence/version deltas, checkpoint-map patching, thread-ID normalization, and sequential supersteps.

citation_format_points.criterion: Material claims have inline `relative/path.py:start-end` citations that resolve at the frozen revision.
Citations cover validation, all three special modes, ordinary updates, and checkpoint persistence.

substantive_logic_points.criterion: Covers scalar-to-list normalization, conversion through LangChain messages/chunks, and UUID assignment to missing IDs on both sides.
Explains that the last REMOVE_ALL marker index found in the right side causes an immediate return of only later right-side messages, bypassing ordinary merge and formatting.
Explains left-copy/index construction, in-place replacement for matching IDs, append for new IDs, and preservation of list position for replacements.
Explains tombstoning of existing IDs, later non-remove replacement clearing the tombstone, final filtering, and the ValueError for removing an absent ID.
Distinguishes OpenAI formatting via `_format_messages`, rejection of any other truthy format, and unchanged merged-message return for a falsey format.
